summary: A 1953 L-4 cab on a stone base atop St. Mary Peak in the Selway-Bitterroot Wilderness, closed in 1972, now staffed by summer volunteers; first-lookout dates disagree.

facts.design: 1936-pattern L-4 hip-roof cab (14 x 14 ft) on a stone base, completed 1953

access.note: Reached only on foot by trail in the Selway-Bitterroot Wilderness; volunteers host visitors in summer. No closure was found in the sources read.

visit.trail_note: A 3.8-mile trail climbs to the summit, according to the volunteer history.

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Bitterroot National Forest (Stevensville Ranger District)

corrections.proposed: remove; no source gives a total height for the current structure
corrections.why: 12.2 m (40 ft) matches the 40-foot pole tower of the 1931/1934 lookout that blew down in 1951, not the current 14 x 14 ft cab on an 8-10 ft stone base.

events.note: NHLR and firelookout.com date a 40-ft pole tower with an L-4 cab to 1931. A 1982 memo cited in the nomination dates the first known fire report from the site to 1931.
Forest improved the site with a lookout house on a 40-ft pole tower (nomination). The volunteer history says CCC built a 50-ft tower in 1934.
Earliest named lookout on firelookout.com's list (Bob Brown, 1942-1943). Staffing before 1952 is disputed.
Violent windstorm blew the cab 100 ft down the mountain (nomination); volunteer history says high winds destroyed the lookout in spring 1951.
Current 1936-pattern L-4 cab on a stone base completed for $4,970; replaced the earlier lookout structure. Firelookout.com says 1952.
August 1956 inspection by the Assistant Forest Supervisor; regional inspectors began to question the lookout's usefulness for detecting fires in the Bitterroot Valley.
Forest Service closed the lookout because of visibility problems from fog and low clouds, and because of rocky alpine terrain in its viewshed (volunteer history).
Unpaid volunteers stationed at the lookout from 1975 (nomination). This conflicts with the 1972 closure in the volunteer history.
Staffed intermittently by paid staff and volunteers from 1977 until 2009 (volunteer history).
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register, November 27, 1992.
Volunteers working under the Passport in Time program restored the exterior.
Cedar shingle roof replaced in kind.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: 1931 (NHLR, firelookout.com, and the 1982 memo) versus 1934 (nomination and volunteer history). The story reports both; the nomination dates the 1934 action to the forest improving the site, not necessarily the first tower.
NHLR, firelookout.com and the nomination say 40 ft; the volunteer history says 50 ft.
Firelookout.com says 1952; the NHLR, nomination and volunteer history say 1953 (the volunteer history gives 1952-1953).
The nomination says an 8-foot stone base, the NHLR says 10 feet, and firelookout.com describes an 8-foot timber tower later enclosed with stone.
The volunteer history says staffed until the 1972 closure; the nomination says unpaid volunteers from 1975; firelookout.com marks 1971 as not staffed. Not resolved.
The record's 2816.7 m matches the NHLR's 9,241 ft. The nomination, firelookout.com and the volunteer history say 9,351 ft (about 2,850 m). Record kept as is; flagged for the editor.

notes_for_editor: The record's height_m 12.2 is the 1931/1934 pole tower, not the current structure; correction proposed. The record's kind two_story is not supported by the sources read, which describe a 14 x 14 ft cab on a stone base; consider revising. The record's elevation_m uses the NHLR figure, while three other sources say 9,351 ft; flagged. The NRHP asset page lists NRIS 100002299, but the listing date was not in the sources read. Staffing as_of is the nomination (form dated January 31, 2018). Access public is inferred from the trail and volunteer hosting, not a posted status. No photos added. Fact-check 2026-10-08: the story's 'still uses volunteers' is now dated to the 2018 nomination, and evidence was added for the 1934 volunteer-history date and the nomination date.
